title: Stream of Characters
description:
Design an algorithm that accepts a stream of characters and checks whether any suffix of the characters queried so far forms a string from a given array of strings `words`.

For example, if `words = ["abc", "xyz"]` and the stream adds one by one `'a'`, `'x'`, `'y'`, `'z'`, your algorithm should detect that the suffix `"xyz"` of the queried characters `"axyz"` matches `"xyz"` from `words`.

Implement the `StreamChecker` class:
- `StreamChecker(String[] words)` initializes the object with the array `words`.
- `boolean query(char letter)` accepts a new character from the stream and returns `true` if any non-empty suffix from the stream forms a word in `words`, and `false` otherwise.
constraints: words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
letter is a lowercase English letter.
At most 4 * 10^4 calls will be made to query.
hints: Checking suffixes of a growing stream is equivalent to checking prefixes of the reversed stream.
Insert every word in reversed order into a trie, and record the maximum word length L.
Keep only the last L queried characters in a buffer. On each query, walk backwards from the newest character through the reversed trie and return true as soon as you hit a word-end node.

examples.explanation: The stream receives a, b, c, d (matches "cd"), e, f (matches "f"), g, h, i, j, k, l (matches "kl").
As characters arrive, "aaab" matches on the 6th query, "ba" on the 7th, "ab" on the 8th, "ba" on the 9th, and "ab"/"abab" on the 10th.

timeComplexity: O(W * L) build, O(L) per query
